Model specification - Standard Detection Probability

Source: vignettes/coa_standard_gaussian_model.Rmd
coa_standard_gaussian_model.Rmd

Overview

COA_Standard_gaussian is a Bayesian Center of Activity (COA) model that estimates the latent spatial position of each individual at each discrete time step from binomial detection counts recorded at an array of fixed receivers. Detection probability decays with squared distance from the individual’s activity center, which corresponds to a Gaussian (half-normal) detection function in distance-sampling terms. The “Standard” variant holds the detection-probability intercept α0\alpha_0 fixed across individuals and time steps (i.e., a single shared intercept), distinguishing it from hierarchical or covariate-extended variants of the model.

NN nind Number of individuals

TT ntime Number of discrete time steps
KK ntrans Number of expected transmissions per time step
yi,t,ry_{i,t,r} y[i, t, r] Detections of individual ii at receiver rr during time step tt, yi,t,r∈{0,1,…,K}y_{i,t,r} \in \{0, 1, \dots, K\}
xr,yrx_r, y_r recX[r], recY[r] Fixed coordinates of receiver rr
[xmin,xmax][x_{\min}, x_{\max}] xlim Spatial bounds of the study area (easting)
[ymin,ymax][y_{\min}, y_{\max}] ylim Spatial bounds of the study area (northing)

for i=1,…,Ni = 1, \dots, N, t=1,…,Tt = 1, \dots, T, r=1,…,Rr = 1, \dots, R.

Parameters

Symbol Stan name Constraint Description
α0\alpha_0 alpha0 α0∈[−5,5]\alpha_0 \in [-5, 5] Detection-probability intercept (logit scale), shared across all individuals and time steps
α1\alpha_1 alpha1 α1>0\alpha_1 > 0 Coefficient governing decline in detection probability with squared distance
sx,i,ts_{x,i,t} sx[i, t] sx,i,t∈[xmin,xmax]s_{x,i,t} \in [x_{\min}, x_{\max}] Easting coordinate of individual ii’s activity center at time tt
sy,i,ts_{y,i,t} sy[i, t] sy,i,t∈[ymin,ymax]s_{y,i,t} \in [y_{\min}, y_{\max}] Northing coordinate of individual ii’s activity center at time tt

The activity center for individual ii at time tt is the latent point 𝐬i,t=(sx,i,t,sy,i,t)\mathbf{s}_{i,t} = (s_{x,i,t},\, s_{y,i,t}).

Distance

For individual ii at time tt, the squared Euclidean distance to receiver rr is

di,t,r2=(xr−sx,i,t)2+(yr−sy,i,t)2. d^2_{i,t,r} \;=\; \bigl(x_r - s_{x,i,t}\bigr)^2 \;+\; \bigl(y_r - s_{y,i,t}\bigr)^2 .

In the Stan code this is the vector d2, computed once per individual–time combination across all receivers. The logistic flag in transformed data is set to 0 for this model, so the working distance term used in the linear predictor is the squared distance itself,

di,t,r=di,t,r2, d_{i,t,r} \;=\; d^2_{i,t,r},

rather than its square root. (When logistic = 1, an alternate model variant instead uses di,t,r=di,t,r2d_{i,t,r} = \sqrt{d^2_{i,t,r}}; that branch is not exercised here.)

Likelihood

Detections at each receiver are modeled as binomial counts out of KK trials, with detection probability governed by a logit-linear function of squared distance from the activity center:

yi,t,r∼Binomial(K,pi,t,r),logit(pi,t,r)=α0−α1di,t,r2, y_{i,t,r} \;\sim\; \mathrm{Binomial}\bigl(K,\; p_{i,t,r}\bigr), \qquad \mathrm{logit}\bigl(p_{i,t,r}\bigr) \;=\; \alpha_0 - \alpha_1 \, d^2_{i,t,r},

equivalently

pi,t,r=logit−1(α0−α1di,t,r2)=11+exp⁡[−(α0−α1di,t,r2)]. p_{i,t,r} \;=\; \mathrm{logit}^{-1}\!\bigl(\alpha_0 - \alpha_1\, d^2_{i,t,r}\bigr) \;=\; \frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\bigl[-(\alpha_0 - \alpha_1\, d^2_{i,t,r})\bigr]} .

This is implemented via Stan’s binomial_logit, which parameterizes the binomial directly on the logit scale for numerical stability:

yi,t,r∼BinomialLogit(K,α0−α1di,t,r2). y_{i,t,r} \;\sim\; \mathrm{BinomialLogit}\bigl(K,\; \alpha_0 - \alpha_1\, d^2_{i,t,r}\bigr).

The full log-likelihood, summed over all individuals, time steps, and receivers, is

log⁡L(α0,α1,𝐬∣𝐲)=∑t=1T∑i=1N∑r=1Rlog⁡BinomialLogit(yi,t,r∣K,α0−α1di,t,r2). \log L(\alpha_0, \alpha_1, \mathbf{s} \mid \mathbf{y}) \;=\; \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{r=1}^{R} \log \mathrm{BinomialLogit}\bigl(y_{i,t,r} \mid K,\; \alpha_0 - \alpha_1 d^2_{i,t,r}\bigr).

Priors

α0∼Cauchy(0,2.5),truncated to [−5,5]α1∼Cauchy(0,2.5),truncated to (0,∞)sx,i,t∼Uniform(xmin,xmax)for all i,tsy,i,t∼Uniform(ymin,ymax)for all i,t \begin{aligned} \alpha_0 &\sim \mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\, 2.5), &&\text{truncated to } [-5, 5] \\ \alpha_1 &\sim \mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\, 2.5), &&\text{truncated to } (0, \infty) \\ s_{x,i,t} &\sim \mathrm{Uniform}(x_{\min},\, x_{\max}) &&\text{for all } i, t \\ s_{y,i,t} &\sim \mathrm{Uniform}(y_{\min},\, y_{\max}) &&\text{for all } i, t \end{aligned}

The Cauchy priors on α0\alpha_0 and α1\alpha_1 are weakly informative and regularize the intercept and decay-rate parameters toward zero while allowing heavy tails. Because both parameters carry explicit lower/upper bounds in the parameters block, the priors are implicitly truncated to those bounds — Stan automatically renormalizes the density over the constrained support, so no separate normalizing constant needs to be added by hand. The activity-center coordinates sx,i,ts_{x,i,t} and sy,i,ts_{y,i,t} have no explicit sampling statement, so they receive Stan’s implicit flat (uniform) prior over their bounded support [xmin,xmax][x_{\min}, x_{\max}] and [ymin,ymax][y_{\min}, y_{\max}], respectively.

Joint posterior

Combining the likelihood and priors, the (unnormalized) joint posterior density is

p(α0,α1,𝐬∣𝐲)∝Cauchy(α0∣0,2.5)⋅Cauchy(α1∣0,2.5)×∏t=1T∏i=1N∏r=1RBinomialLogit(yi,t,r∣K,α0−α1di,t,r2(𝐬i,t)), \begin{aligned} p(\alpha_0, \alpha_1, \mathbf{s} \mid \mathbf{y}) \;\propto\;\; & \mathrm{Cauchy}(\alpha_0 \mid 0, 2.5) \cdot \mathrm{Cauchy}(\alpha_1 \mid 0, 2.5) \\[4pt] \times\;\; & \prod_{t=1}^{T} \prod_{i=1}^{N} \prod_{r=1}^{R} \mathrm{BinomialLogit}\bigl(y_{i,t,r} \mid K,\; \alpha_0 - \alpha_1 d^2_{i,t,r}(\mathbf{s}_{i,t})\bigr), \end{aligned}

subject to α0∈[−5,5]\alpha_0 \in [-5, 5], α1>0\alpha_1 > 0, sx,i,t∈[xmin,xmax]s_{x,i,t} \in [x_{\min}, x_{\max}], and sy,i,t∈[ymin,ymax]s_{y,i,t} \in [y_{\min}, y_{\max}] for all i,ti, t.

Generated quantities

Two derived quantities are computed from the posterior draws of α0\alpha_0 and α1\alpha_1:

Baseline detection probability. The detection probability at distance zero (i.e., when the activity center coincides exactly with a receiver):

p0=logit−1(α0)=11+e−α0. p_0 \;=\; \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_0) \;=\; \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\alpha_0}}.

Detection-decay standard deviation. The squared-distance decay term α1d2\alpha_1 d^2 is the kernel of a Gaussian (half-normal) detection function. Writing the decay term in the conventional distance-sampling form d2/(2σ2)d^2 / (2\sigma^2) and matching coefficients,

α1=12σ2⇔σ=12α1, \alpha_1 \;=\; \frac{1}{2\sigma^2} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \sigma \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{1}{2\alpha_1}},

so that the detection function can equivalently be written as

pi,t,r=logit−1(α0−di,t,r22σ2). p_{i,t,r} \;=\; \mathrm{logit}^{-1}\!\left(\alpha_0 - \frac{d^2_{i,t,r}}{2\sigma^2}\right).

Here σ\sigma has units of distance and characterizes the effective spatial range of detection: it is the standard deviation of the Gaussian decay in detection log-odds with distance from the activity center, with larger σ\sigma corresponding to a more slowly-decaying (longer-range) detection function.
